# az-tf-mlz-connectivity-hub

The hub-and-spoke topology of Fortytwo's managed landing zone (MLZ), in AzAPI: one hub virtual network per
region, each in its own resource group, with its Azure Firewall, NAT gateway, Azure Bastion, DNS private
resolver and virtual network gateways, the hubs peered with each other and routed through their
firewalls. It replaces the azurerm-based `avm-ptn-alz-connectivity-hub-and-spoke-vnet`; its building
blocks are MLZ modules and AVM's AzAPI modules.

| Resource | From |
|---|---|
| One resource group per hub (and one for the private DNS zones) | this module |
| Hub virtual networks, their subnets and the peerings between hubs | `Azure/avm-res-network-virtualnetwork/azurerm` 0.22.3 (AzAPI) |
| Route tables of `AzureFirewallSubnet` and `GatewaySubnet`, with their routes | `Azure/avm-ptn-alz-sub-vending/azure//modules/route-table` 0.3.4 (AzAPI) |
| Firewall and policy, with their public IP addresses | [`az-tf-mlz-azure-firewall`](https://github.com/fortytwoservices/az-tf-mlz-azure-firewall) |
| NAT gateway on `AzureFirewallSubnet` | [`az-tf-mlz-nat-gateway`](https://github.com/fortytwoservices/az-tf-mlz-nat-gateway) |
| Azure Bastion | [`az-tf-mlz-bastion`](https://github.com/fortytwoservices/az-tf-mlz-bastion) |
| DNS private resolver and its endpoints | [`az-tf-mlz-dns-resolver`](https://github.com/fortytwoservices/az-tf-mlz-dns-resolver) |
| VPN and ExpressRoute gateways, sites and connections | [`az-tf-mlz-virtual-network-gateway`](https://github.com/fortytwoservices/az-tf-mlz-virtual-network-gateway) |
| Private Link private DNS zones, linked to every hub | `Azure/avm-ptn-network-private-link-private-dns-zones/azurerm` 0.23.2 (AzAPI) |
| Names from a template | `Azure/avm-utl-naming/azure` 0.2.0, `Azure/avm-utl-regions/azurerm` 0.13.0 |

Spokes are created and peered by subscription vending, which reads the `connectivity` output (the contract
shared with `az-tf-mlz-connectivity-vwan`: hub network IDs, firewall address and policy, DNS servers, the
spokes' default route). Firewall rules live in a rules state that calls the firewall module's
`//modules/rule_collection_group` with the policy ID from that output, so a rule change never plans the
hubs. The DDoS protection plan is the connectivity root's: pass its ID.

## How it behaves

The design follows the Cloud Adoption Framework's "Traditional Azure networking topology", the
Architecture Center's "Hub-spoke network topology in Azure" and Azure Firewall's "Use Azure Firewall to
route a multi-hub and spoke topology".

- **Subnets from what a hub has:** `AzureFirewallSubnet` and, for Basic or forced tunnelling,
  `AzureFirewallManagementSubnet`; `GatewaySubnet` with a gateway; `AzureBastionSubnet` with Bastion; the
  resolver's two delegated subnets. Workloads and shared services belong in spokes, not in the hub.
- **Routing.** The firewall's private address is its subnet's fifth address, known before apply (the
  module checks Azure's). `AzureFirewallSubnet` sends `0.0.0.0/0` to the Internet, or for forced
  tunnelling to an appliance, the VPN gateway, or nowhere so a BGP-learned default applies (the management
  NIC is required then), and each other region's `routing_supernet` to that region's firewall.
  `GatewaySubnet` sends each spoke's exact prefix (`spoke_address_prefixes`) and the other regions to the
  hub's firewall, so traffic from on-premises is inspected both ways: add a spoke's prefix before vending
  it. Both keep gateway route propagation on. Spokes get `spoke_default_routes` from the contract, with
  propagation off.
- **The mesh.** Every pair of hubs is peered both ways, with forwarded traffic allowed and no gateway
  transit between hubs (`mesh_peering_enabled`). Microsoft recommends this for two regions and Virtual WAN
  beyond.
- **DNS.** A created firewall policy proxies DNS to the resolver's inbound endpoint, at its subnet's fifth
  address (except on Basic, which has no DNS proxy); the contract's `dns_servers` is then the firewall's
  address, else the resolver's. The hub virtual network keeps Azure-provided DNS unless
  `virtual_network_dns_servers` is set, as Microsoft recommends where a VPN gateway lives.
- **Names.** Each component takes an explicit name; without one, `naming` makes it from a template, with
  the hub region's short name as the `region` token and this module's catalogue additions for the
  resources a hub has several of (public IP addresses, route tables).
- **Serialisation and timing.** Writes to a virtual network (subnets, peerings) are serialised on it. A
  VPN gateway takes 20 to 60 minutes per write and a firewall tens of minutes, so `timeouts` default to 90
  minutes, and `retry` covers the transient errors of all the modules called. A gateway write that fails
  with `VmssGatewayDeploymentFailed` ("intermittent error") succeeds when the apply is run again.

Not in this release: locks and role assignments on the components, NSGs, IP address management, Route
Server, Virtual Network Manager, and re-syncing the peerings after a hub's address space changes.

## Required Inputs

The following input variables are required:

### <a name="input_hub_virtual_networks"></a> [hub\_virtual\_networks](#input\_hub\_virtual\_networks)

Description: The hub virtual networks, keyed by region key (the key of the region's entry in the `connectivity` output, usually the region's name). Exactly one is primary: the private DNS zones live in its region. Each hub gets a resource group of its own (Cloud Adoption Framework: each region's hub resources in their own resource group). Every name is optional: an explicit name wins, else `naming` makes one. Subnets are created for the components that are set; workloads do not belong in the hub (Microsoft Learn, "Use Azure Firewall to route a multi-hub and spoke topology"), so there are no others.

- `location` - Azure region of the hub and of everything in its resource group.
- `address_space` - The hub virtual network's address ranges, holding the subnets below.
- `is_primary` - (Optional) Whether this is the primary region. Exactly one hub is. Defaults to `false`.
- `name` - (Optional) Name of the hub virtual network.
- `resource_group_name` - (Optional) Name of the resource group the module creates for the hub and its resources.
- `routing_supernet` - (Optional) The region's summary address ranges (its hub and spokes). Other hubs route them to this hub's firewall, and they are published in the `connectivity` output.
- `spoke_address_prefixes` - (Optional) The address spaces of this region's spokes, keyed by a stable name. With a firewall and a gateway, the `GatewaySubnet` route table sends each to the firewall, so traffic from on-premises is inspected both ways. They must be the spokes' exact prefixes: a summary loses to the peerings' more specific system routes (Microsoft Learn). Add a spoke's prefix here before vending it.
- `virtual_network_dns_servers` - (Optional) Custom DNS servers of the hub virtual network. Null (the default) keeps Azure-provided DNS, which Microsoft recommends in a gateway's virtual network (VPN Gateway FAQ). Set it, for example to the resolver's inbound address, for point-to-site clients to resolve private DNS zones; the servers must forward to Azure DNS (168.63.129.16), as the resolver and a firewall DNS proxy do.
- `gateway_subnet_address_prefix` - (Optional) Address prefix of `GatewaySubnet`, required with a gateway: /27 or larger, /26 or larger for `ErGwScale` or for a VPN and an ExpressRoute gateway together (Microsoft Learn recommends /26).
- `gateway_route_table_name` - (Optional) Name of the `GatewaySubnet` route table, created for a hub with a firewall and a gateway.
- `firewall` - (Optional) An Azure Firewall through `az-tf-mlz-azure-firewall`, in an `AzureFirewallSubnet` the module creates:
  - `name` - (Optional) Name of the firewall.
  - `sku_tier` - (Optional) `Basic`, `Standard` (default) or `Premium`.
  - `zones` - (Optional) Availability zones of the firewall. Null leaves them out (Microsoft: none for Basic).
  - `subnet_address_prefix` - Address prefix of `AzureFirewallSubnet`, /26 or larger. The firewall's private address is its fifth address (`cidrhost(prefix, 4)`), which the routes use and the module checks against Azure's.
  - `management_subnet_address_prefix` - (Optional) Address prefix of `AzureFirewallManagementSubnet` (/26 or larger): the management NIC, required for Basic and for forced tunnelling. Adding or removing it replaces the firewall.
  - `public_ip_name`, `management_public_ip_name` - (Optional) Names of the public IP addresses the module creates for the firewall and its management NIC.
  - `route_table_name` - (Optional) Name of the `AzureFirewallSubnet` route table.
  - `default_route` - (Optional) The firewall subnet's default route: `next_hop_type` `Internet` (default), or for forced tunnelling `VirtualAppliance` (with `next_hop_ip_address`) or `VirtualNetworkGateway`; `enabled = false` sends no default route, so a default route learned through BGP from the gateway applies. Anything but `Internet` needs the management NIC (Microsoft Learn, "Azure Firewall forced tunneling").
  - `firewall_policy_id` - (Optional) Resource ID of an existing firewall policy. When set, the module creates no policy and `firewall_policy` is ignored.
  - `firewall_policy` - (Optional) The policy the module creates, with the firewall's tier: `name`, `base_policy_id` (a parent policy in the same region), `threat_intelligence_mode` (`Alert` by default, `Deny` or `Off`; Basic is alert-only), `dns_proxy_enabled` (default: on, except on Basic) and `dns_servers` (default: the hub resolver's inbound address, else Azure DNS). A Basic policy takes neither: it has no DNS settings at all. Rules are not set here: a rules state calls the firewall module's `//modules/rule_collection_group` with the `firewall_policy_id` from the `connectivity` output.
- `nat_gateway` - (Optional) A NAT gateway through `az-tf-mlz-nat-gateway` on `AzureFirewallSubnet`, the firewall's outbound path (Microsoft Learn: up to 16 public IPs, far more SNAT ports); needs `firewall`. `sku_name` `StandardV2` (default, zone-redundant: the one for a zone-redundant firewall) or `Standard` with at most one zone in `zones`; `idle_timeout_in_minutes` (4 to 120); `name` and `public_ip_name` of the public IP address the module creates for it.
- `bastion` - (Optional) Azure Bastion through `az-tf-mlz-bastion`, in an `AzureBastionSubnet` the module creates from `subnet_address_prefix` (/26 or larger), with a public IP address it creates (`public_ip_name`). `sku` is `Basic`, `Standard` (default) or `Premium`: all reach VMs in peered virtual networks; Developer is not offered (no peering, no subnet). `zones`, `scale_units` and the feature flags are the Bastion module's, with its defaults.
- `dns_resolver` - (Optional) A DNS private resolver through `az-tf-mlz-dns-resolver`, with an inbound endpoint in a subnet the module creates from `inbound_subnet_address_prefix` (/28 to /24, delegated to the resolver) at its fifth address (`cidrhost(prefix, 4)`), and an outbound endpoint when `outbound_subnet_address_prefix` is set. Forwarding rulesets are the caller's: call `//modules/forwarding_ruleset` of the resolver module with the outbound endpoint's ID (do not link a ruleset that forwards to the inbound endpoint to the hub: Learn, a DNS loop).
- `vpn_gateway` - (Optional) A VPN gateway through `az-tf-mlz-virtual-network-gateway` in `GatewaySubnet`: `name`, `sku` (`VpnGw1AZ` default to `VpnGw5AZ`), `vpn_generation`, `active_active`, `bgp` and `point_to_site` as that module takes them. The module creates its IP configurations (`ipconfig1`, `ipconfig2` when active-active, `ipconfig3` for point-to-site on an active-active gateway) and their public IP addresses, named by `public_ip_names` in that order, else by the template. `local_network_gateways` (sites) and `connections` are that module's, without their own locks, role assignments and diagnostic settings; connection keys come from `connection_secrets`.
- `express_route_gateway` - (Optional) An ExpressRoute gateway through `az-tf-mlz-virtual-network-gateway` in `GatewaySubnet` (Azure assigns its public IP address): `name`, `sku` (`ErGw1AZ` default, `ErGw2AZ`, `ErGw3AZ` or `ErGwScale` with `express_route_scale_units`), and `connections` to circuits (`express_route_circuit_id`; an authorization key, for a circuit in another subscription, through `connection_secrets`). A VPN and an ExpressRoute gateway can share `GatewaySubnet`; the gateway module has not tested that.

### <a name="input_parent_id"></a> [parent\_id](#input\_parent\_id)

Description: Resource ID of the connectivity subscription (`/subscriptions/<id>`). The module creates one resource group in it per hub, and one for the private DNS zones.

Type: `string`

## Optional Inputs

The following input variables are optional (have default values):

### <a name="input_connection_secrets"></a> [connection\_secrets](#input\_connection\_secrets)

Description: (Optional) The gateways' connection keys, keyed `<hub key>/<connection key>`: the pre-shared key of each `IPsec` or `Vnet2Vnet` connection (required), and the authorization key of an ExpressRoute connection to a circuit in another subscription. Ephemeral and write-only: sent to Azure, never stored in state; change the connection's `secret_version` to send a new key.

Type: `map(string)`

Default: `{}`

### <a name="input_ddos_protection_plan_id"></a> [ddos\_protection\_plan\_id](#input\_ddos\_protection\_plan\_id)

Description: (Optional) Resource ID of an existing DDoS protection plan, applied to every hub virtual network and published per region in the `connectivity` output for subscription vending. The Cloud Adoption Framework asks for one plan in the connectivity subscription for every virtual network; it is created by the connectivity root, not here, because it serves the whole tenant and is billed by the month.

Type: `string`

Default: `null`

### <a name="input_diagnostic_settings"></a> [diagnostic\_settings](#input\_diagnostic\_settings)

Description: A map of diagnostic settings to create on each hub's Azure Firewall, Azure Bastion, DNS private resolver and virtual network gateways. Azure offers no log categories on the resolver, so it receives each setting with `logs` removed, and none that has no `metrics`. The hub virtual networks, the firewall policies, the NAT gateways, the route tables and the gateway connections get none from this module. The map key is deliberately arbitrary to avoid issues where map keys maybe unknown at plan time.

- `name` - (Optional) The name of the diagnostic setting. One will be generated if not set, however this will not be unique if you want to create multiple diagnostic setting resources.
- `logs` - (Optional) A set of log entries to send to the destination. Each entry has the following attributes:
  - `category` - (Optional) The name of a specific log category to enable. Mutually exclusive with `category_group`.
  - `category_group` - (Optional) The name of a log category group to enable (for example, `allLogs` or `audit`). Mutually exclusive with `category`.
  - `enabled` - (Optional) Whether the log entry is enabled. Defaults to `true`.
  - `retention_policy` - (Optional) The retention policy for the log entry.
    - `days` - (Optional) The retention period in days. Defaults to `0` (retain indefinitely).
    - `enabled` - (Optional) Whether the retention policy is enabled. Defaults to `false`.
- `metrics` - (Optional) A set of metric entries to send to the destination. Each entry has the following attributes:
  - `category` - (Optional) The name of the metric category to enable.
  - `enabled` - (Optional) Whether the metric entry is enabled. Defaults to `true`.
  - `retention_policy` - (Optional) The retention policy for the metric entry, with the same `days` and `enabled` attributes as `logs.retention_policy`.
- `log_analytics_destination_type` - (Optional) The destination type for the diagnostic setting. Possible values are `Dedicated` and `AzureDiagnostics`. Defaults to `Dedicated`.
- `workspace_resource_id` - (Optional) The resource ID of the log analytics workspace to send logs and metrics to.
- `storage_account_resource_id` - (Optional) The resource ID of the storage account to send logs and metrics to.
- `event_hub_authorization_rule_resource_id` - (Optional) The resource ID of the event hub authorization rule to send logs and metrics to.
- `event_hub_name` - (Optional) The name of the event hub. If none is specified, the default event hub will be selected.
- `marketplace_partner_resource_id` - (Optional) The full ARM resource ID of the Marketplace resource to which you would like to send Diagnostic Logs.

map(object({
    name = optional(string, null)
    logs = optional(set(object({

### <a name="input_ignore_body_changes"></a> [ignore\_body\_changes](#input\_ignore\_body\_changes)

Description: Paths in each resource's `body` whose changes the AzAPI provider ignores. Prefer Terraform's `lifecycle.ignore_changes` when the paths are static; use this variable when the paths must be derived from variables or other non-static values.

Paths use dot notation, for example `properties.dhcpOptions`. Individual list items cannot be targeted; ignore the whole list property instead. Configuration changes at an ignored path are **not** sent to Azure until that path is removed from the list. Changes take effect only after an apply, because the value is held in provider-private state.

- `resources_resource_groups` - Ignored body paths for the resource groups.
- `network_virtual_networks` - Slot for the hub virtual networks, `Azure/avm-res-network-virtualnetwork/azurerm`'s `ignore_body_changes`; the hub peerings use its `virtual_networks_virtual_network_peerings` slot.
- `network_azure_firewalls` - Slot for `az-tf-mlz-azure-firewall`, shaped like its `ignore_body_changes`.
- `network_nat_gateways` - Slot for `az-tf-mlz-nat-gateway`, shaped like its `ignore_body_changes`.
- `network_bastion_hosts` - Slot for `az-tf-mlz-bastion`, shaped like its `ignore_body_changes`.
- `network_dns_resolvers` - Slot for `az-tf-mlz-dns-resolver`, shaped like its `ignore_body_changes` (without the rulesets, which this module does not create).
- `network_virtual_network_gateways` - Slot for `az-tf-mlz-virtual-network-gateway` (the VPN and the ExpressRoute gateways), shaped like its `ignore_body_changes`.

The route tables (`Azure/avm-ptn-alz-sub-vending/azure//modules/route-table`) and the private DNS zones (`Azure/avm-ptn-network-private-link-private-dns-zones/azurerm`) take no ignored paths.

### <a name="input_mesh_peering_enabled"></a> [mesh\_peering\_enabled](#input\_mesh\_peering\_enabled)

Description: (Optional) Whether every pair of hubs is peered both ways (forwarded traffic allowed, no gateway transit between hubs), with each hub's `AzureFirewallSubnet` routing the other regions' `routing_supernet` to their firewalls and its `GatewaySubnet` routing them to its own firewall (Microsoft Learn, "Use Azure Firewall to route a multi-hub and spoke topology"). The Cloud Adoption Framework recommends global peering to connect two regions' hubs and Virtual WAN beyond two regions. `false` leaves the hubs unpeered, for example when ExpressRoute connects them. Defaults to `true`.

Type: `bool`

Default: `true`

### <a name="input_naming"></a> [naming](#input\_naming)

Description: (Optional) A naming template for every component left without an explicit name, through `Azure/avm-utl-naming/azure` v0.2.0, called once per hub. Null: every component needs an explicit name.

- `template` - The module's `naming_templates.name`, with tokens escaped (`$${slug}` in HCL passes `${slug}`). The module adds a `region` token, the hub region's short name (`geo_code` from `Azure/avm-utl-regions`, for example `sdc` for swedencentral): use it, or the names of two hubs collide. Example: `"az$${separator}$${slug}$${separator}$${landing_zone}$${separator}$${environment}$${separator}$${region}$${separator}$${instance}"`.
- `variables` - (Optional) More template tokens, for example `{ landing_zone = "conn", environment = "pd" }`. Not the naming module's own tokens (`name`, `prefix`, `suffix`, `slug`, `separator`, `unique`, `unique_seed`, `instance`, `terraform_key`, `resource_type`, `variant`, `min_length`, `max_length`), which it refuses, nor `region`, which this module sets.
- `instance` - (Optional) The instance number, formatted as `001`.
- `slug_overrides` - (Optional) Slugs by catalogue key, for example `{ public_ip_address_firewall = "pipfw" }`.
- `custom_override_file` - (Optional) Path of a catalogue override file (`custom_override_file` of the naming module). Defaults to this module's `naming-overrides.json`, which lets NAT gateway names have hyphens and adds the keys below for resources a hub has several of; a file of your own must carry them too.

Catalogue keys used: `resource_group`, `virtual_network`, `azure_firewall`, `firewall_policy`, `nat_gateway`, `bastion_host`, `dns_resolver`, `dns_resolver_inbound_endpoint`, `dns_resolver_outbound_endpoint`, `virtual_network_gateway`, `virtual_network_gateway_express_route_gateway`, and from this module's override file `public_ip_address_firewall` (slug `pip-afw`), `public_ip_address_firewall_management` (`pip-afwm`), `public_ip_address_nat_gateway` (`pip-ng`), `public_ip_address_bastion` (`pip-bas`), `public_ip_address_vpn_gateway_1` to `_3` (`pip-vgw1` to `pip-vgw3`), `route_table_firewall` (`rt-afw`), `route_table_gateway` (`rt-vgw`) and `resource_group_private_dns` (`rg-pdns`).

Type:

```hcl
object({
    template             = string
    variables            = optional(map(string), {})
    instance             = optional(number)
    slug_overrides       = optional(map(string))
    custom_override_file = optional(string)
  })
```

Default: `null`

### <a name="input_private_dns_zones"></a> [private\_dns\_zones](#input\_private\_dns\_zones)

Description: (Optional) The Private Link private DNS zones, through `Azure/avm-ptn-network-private-link-private-dns-zones/azurerm` v0.23.2, in one resource group the module creates in the primary hub's region, each linked to every hub virtual network (where the resolver resolves them). Null (the default) creates none: keep them in a state of their own and link them to each region's `hub_virtual_network_id`.

- `resource_group_name` - (Optional) Name of their resource group. Defaults to the primary hub's template name for the `resource_group_private_dns` key.
- `zone_name_filter` - (Optional) A regular expression: only zones whose name (as the pattern lists it, with `{regionName}` and `{regionCode}` placeholders) matches are created, in the primary hub's region only. Null: every zone for the primary region, plus each other hub's regional zones.
- `excluded_zones` - (Optional) Zone names or keys of the pattern's list to leave out.
- `additional_zones` - (Optional) More zones for the primary region, by a stable key.

Type:

```hcl
object({
    resource_group_name = optional(string)
    zone_name_filter    = optional(string)
    excluded_zones      = optional(list(string), [])
    additional_zones    = optional(map(string), {})
  })
```

Default: `null`

### <a name="input_resource_types"></a> [resource\_types](#input\_resource\_types)

Description: Override the AzAPI `<provider>/<resource>@<api-version>` strings used by this module and the modules it calls. Each key defaults to a tested value; supply only the keys you want to override.

- `resources_resource_groups` - The resource groups.
- `network_route_tables` - Slot for `Azure/avm-ptn-alz-sub-vending/azure//modules/route-table`: `this` (the route tables) and `route` (their routes). Defaults live in that module.
- `network_azure_firewalls` - Slot for `az-tf-mlz-azure-firewall`, shaped like its `resource_types`. Defaults live in that module.
- `network_nat_gateways` - Slot for `az-tf-mlz-nat-gateway`, shaped like its `resource_types`. Defaults live in that module.
- `network_bastion_hosts` - Slot for `az-tf-mlz-bastion`, shaped like its `resource_types`. Defaults live in that module.
- `network_dns_resolvers` - Slot for `az-tf-mlz-dns-resolver`, shaped like its `resource_types` (without the rulesets). Defaults live in that module.
- `network_virtual_network_gateways` - Slot for `az-tf-mlz-virtual-network-gateway` (the VPN and the ExpressRoute gateways), shaped like its `resource_types`. Defaults live in that module.

The hub virtual networks and their peerings use `Azure/avm-res-network-virtualnetwork/azurerm` v0.22.3's fixed `2024-07-01`; the private DNS zones use `Azure/avm-ptn-network-private-link-private-dns-zones/azurerm` v0.23.2's own.

### <a name="input_retry"></a> [retry](#input\_retry)

Description: Retry configuration applied to every `azapi` resource managed by the module and the modules it calls. The defaults retry what those modules retry by default: `AnotherOperationInProgress` (parallel writes to a virtual network, a route table, a firewall policy or a gateway), `ReferencedResourceNotProvisioned` (a subnet or peering written while its virtual network is still updating) and `CannotDeleteResource` (a resolver deleted right after its endpoints); any field can be overridden.

- `error_message_regex`  - (Optional) A list of regex patterns matching error messages that trigger a retry.
- `interval_seconds`     - (Optional) Initial interval between retries in seconds. Defaults to `30`.
- `max_interval_seconds` - (Optional) Maximum interval between retries in seconds. Defaults to `300`.

See <https://registry.terraform.io/providers/Azure/azapi/latest/docs/resources/resource#retry> for full semantics.

Type:

```hcl
object({
    error_message_regex  = optional(list(string), ["AnotherOperationInProgress", "ReferencedResourceNotProvisioned", "CannotDeleteResource"])
    interval_seconds     = optional(number, 30)
    max_interval_seconds = optional(number, 300)
  })
```

Default: `{}`

### <a name="input_tags"></a> [tags](#input\_tags)

Description: (Optional) Tags of every resource the module creates that takes tags: the resource groups, the hub virtual networks, the route tables, the firewalls and their policies, the NAT gateways, Bastion, the resolvers and their endpoints, the gateways, the public IP addresses of all of these, and the private DNS zones. Peerings, routes, subnets and the gateways' sites and connections take none.

Type: `map(string)`

Default: `null`

### <a name="input_timeouts"></a> [timeouts](#input\_timeouts)

Description: Per-operation timeouts applied to every `azapi` resource managed by the module and the modules it calls. Each value is a Go duration string (e.g. `30m`, `1h`). A VPN gateway write takes up to 45 minutes by Microsoft Learn (62 were seen in the sandbox), a firewall's tens of minutes, so writes default to 90 minutes; any field can be overridden.

- `create` - (Optional) Timeout for create operations. Defaults to `90m`.
- `read`   - (Optional) Timeout for read operations. Defaults to `5m`.
- `update` - (Optional) Timeout for update operations. Defaults to `90m`.
- `delete` - (Optional) Timeout for delete operations. Defaults to `90m`.

Type:

```hcl
object({
    create = optional(string, "90m")
    read   = optional(string, "5m")
    update = optional(string, "90m")
    delete = optional(string, "90m")
  })
```

Default: `{}`

## Outputs

The following outputs are exported:

### <a name="output_connectivity"></a> [connectivity](#output\_connectivity)

Description: The connectivity contract shared with `az-tf-mlz-connectivity-vwan` (same keys; what does not apply to hub and spoke is null), for subscription vending, firewall rules and governance. It holds no secrets: publish it as JSON rather than reading this state.

- `topology` - `hub_and_spoke`.
- `connectivity_subscription_id` - The connectivity subscription's ID.
- `regions` - By `hub_virtual_networks` key: `is_primary`, `routing_supernet`, `hub_virtual_network_id` (spokes peer with it: the hub side allows gateway transit and forwarded traffic, the spoke side uses the remote gateways), `virtual_hub_id` and `vhub_route_table_ids` (null), `routing_intent_enabled` (false), `firewall_private_ip`, `firewall_policy_id`, `dns_servers` (the firewall's address when its DNS proxy is on, else the resolver's inbound address, else empty), `ipam_pool_id` (null), `ddos_protection_plan_id` (`ddos_protection_plan_id`) and `spoke_default_routes`: the routes for a spoke's route table, in `Azure/avm-ptn-alz-sub-vending/azure` v0.3.4's `routes` shape (`0.0.0.0/0` to the firewall; null without a firewall), applied with `bgp_route_propagation_enabled = false` so on-premises prefixes do not bypass the firewall.
- `base_firewall_policy_id` - The primary hub's firewall policy's parent, if any.
- `private_dns_zone_ids` - The private DNS zones' resource IDs by zone name, null without `private_dns_zones`.
- `private_dns_resource_group_id` - Their resource group's ID, null without `private_dns_zones`.

### <a name="output_hub_virtual_networks"></a> [hub\_virtual\_networks](#output\_hub\_virtual\_networks)

Description: What each hub's resources are, by `hub_virtual_networks` key (null where a hub has none):

- `resource_group_id`, `resource_id`, `name` (the hub virtual network), `subnet_resource_ids` (by `firewall`, `firewall_management`, `gateway`, `bastion`, `dns_resolver_inbound`, `dns_resolver_outbound`), `peering_resource_ids` (by remote hub key).
- `firewall_resource_id`, `firewall_private_ip_address` (from Azure), `firewall_public_ip_addresses`, `firewall_policy_resource_id`, `firewall_route_table_resource_id`, `nat_gateway_resource_id`, `nat_gateway_public_ip_addresses`.
- `bastion_resource_id`, `dns_resolver_resource_id`, `dns_resolver_inbound_ip_address`, `dns_resolver_outbound_endpoint_resource_id` (for the caller's forwarding rulesets).
- `vpn_gateway_resource_id`, `vpn_gateway_public_ip_addresses`, `vpn_gateway_bgp_settings` (ASN and peering addresses, for on-premises devices), `vpn_gateway_connection_resource_ids`, `vpn_gateway_local_network_gateway_resource_ids`, `express_route_gateway_resource_id`, `express_route_gateway_connection_resource_ids`, `gateway_route_table_resource_id`.

### <a name="output_name"></a> [name](#output\_name)

Description: Name of the primary hub's virtual network.

### <a name="output_resource_id"></a> [resource\_id](#output\_resource\_id)

Description: Resource ID of the primary hub's virtual network.

## Development

Tools: Terraform 1.17.0, TFLint 0.65.0, terraform-docs 0.24.0 (the versions CI uses).

| What | Command |
|---|---|
| Format, validate, lint, unit tests, README drift (what CI runs) | `scripts/check.sh` |
| Format the code and regenerate the READMEs first | `scripts/check.sh --fix` |
| Integration tests in Azure | `ARM_SUBSCRIPTION_ID=<test subscription> scripts/integration.sh [dir ...]` |
| Examples: apply, plan again (must be empty), destroy | `ARM_SUBSCRIPTION_ID=<test subscription> scripts/e2e.sh [examples/<name> ...]` |

`README.md` files are generated from `_header.md`, the code and `_footer.md`; do not edit them by hand.

## Versions and releases

Every release is a SemVer tag `vX.Y.Z`; tags never move, and `main` is never consumed. Pin a release:

```hcl
source = "git::https://github.com/fortytwoservices/<repository>.git?ref=vX.Y.Z"
```

Pull requests are squash-merged, and their titles follow Conventional Commits, which set the next
version: `fix:` a patch, `feat:` a minor (a patch before 1.0.0), `feat!:` or `fix!:` a major (a minor
before 1.0.0). `docs:`, `test:`, `ci:`, `chore:` and `refactor:` release nothing. release-please keeps a
release pull request open; merging it writes `CHANGELOG.md`, the tag and the GitHub release.
